new_jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, Non-Standard Infrastructure Delivery (NSID)
new_jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------


AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.  

You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  

About the Role  

The AWS Non\-Standard Infrastructure Global Delivery Team builds and scales infrastructure for AWS programs that don't fit neatly into traditional data center models. Our projects are tailored to the specific needs of internal and external customers — from satellite ground stations that downlink data from orbit, to specialized labs where engineers develop custom silicon and push the boundaries of quantum computing, to purpose\-built environments with precision environmental controls for archival storage systems, to infrastructure that extends the AWS network to the furthest edge of its global footprint. Each program brings its own constraints, its own technical requirements, and often its own first\-of\-kind design challenges.  

What makes this team unique is the degree of ambiguity we operate in. Many of our projects begin as loosely defined requests from internal customer teams who know what they need to accomplish but not necessarily what infrastructure it takes to get there. A significant part of this role is working upstream with those customers to develop initial requirements, define technical scope, build demand forecasts, and refine scaling models — often for infrastructure types where no established playbook exists. The solutions we deliver are boutique by nature: custom\-designed to meet specific programmatic needs, site constraints, and operational models that vary from project to project.
  

The scope is broad, the problems are novel, and the pace of growth means we are constantly onboarding new infrastructure types and scaling models.  

If you thrive in ambiguity, enjoy the challenge of translating vague asks into engineered solutions, and want to shape how AWS builds and scales its infrastructure globally — this role is for you.  

We have an immediate opening for a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager III to drive capacity delivery across multiple non\-standard infrastructure programs worldwide. You will lead cross\-functional teams through the full lifecycle of infrastructure delivery — from upstream requirements definition and demand forecasting through design development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment. You will develop and implement scalable mechanisms for tracking program health, drive data\-driven decisions influencing significant capital investments, and work with stakeholders across AWS to solve constraints, remove blockers, and accelerate delivery.  

Your work will span:  

* Requirements development — Working with internal customer teams to translate ambiguous needs into defined technical requirements, scope documents, and infrastructure specifications for novel deployment types
* Stakeholder management and influence — Navigating complex, matrixed organizational structures and influencing without authority to align diverse teams, secure resources, drive decisions, and maintain momentum across programs where no single team owns the end\-to\-end outcome
* Demand forecasting and capacity planning — Building initial demand models and scaling forecasts for programs where historical baselines don't exist, and refining them as programs mature
* Boutique design coordination — Partnering with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions that meet unique programmatic constraints (environmental, regulatory, physical, operational)
* Multi\-year delivery execution — Driving complex, globally distributed projects from conceptual feasibility through budget approval, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning
* Cross\-program coordination — Identifying synergies, shared solutions, and lessons learned across a diverse portfolio of infrastructure types
* Mechanism development — Building scalable processes and reporting to monitor delivery health, drive accountability, and escalate to leadership as the portfolio grows


This role offers an opportunity to drive and influence business\-critical decisions impacting the long\-term future of AWS, working at the leading edge of emerging capability and service offerings. You must be comfortable managing remote project teams delivering novel — and sometimes pioneering — solutions across multiple countries and time zones; operating as the connective tissue between customer teams with undefined needs and engineering teams who build solutions; assessing and mitigating downstream risk; troubleshooting unforeseen implementation issues; removing barriers to project success; and operating effectively amid persistent uncertainty and change.  

Up to 15% domestic and international travel may be necessary to support AWS non\-standard infrastructure planning and scaling efforts.  

  

Key job responsibilities  

* Work upstream with internal customer teams to elicit, define, and document technical requirements for infrastructure programs that are often undefined or loosely scoped at inception
* Develop initial demand forecasts and capacity scaling models for emerging

### **Description**

  

The Senior Project Manager leads the successful delivery of large, complex, or multiple construction projects in the San Fernando Valley, with full accountability for safety, quality, schedule, contract compliance, and financial performance from preconstruction through closeout. This is a daily, on\-site leadership role — you'll be hands\-on with your project teams, clients, and field leadership every day, not managing from a distance.  

You'll mentor Project Managers, Assistant Project Managers, and Project Engineers, build long\-term client relationships, and represent the company as a trusted senior advisor throughout the project lifecycle.  

The role reports to the Project Director, Project Executive, Vice President of Operations, or other assigned supervisor, and works closely with clients, consultants, trade partners, field leadership, and company leadership.  

### **Key Responsibilities**

  

* Champion project safety, quality, scheduling, and risk management across assigned projects, partnering with field leadership on expectations.
* Maintain full accountability for project forecasting, budgeting, billing, cash flow, and overall financial performance.
* Lead administration of prime contracts, subcontracts, purchase orders, and project agreements, directing compliance and change management processes.
* Evaluate cost impacts, forecast variances, and contractual risks; implement corrective actions and support the resolution of claims or disputes.
* Lead, mentor, and develop Project Managers, Assistant Project Managers, Project Engineers, and other project team members.
* Build and maintain long\-term relationships with clients, consultants, subcontractors, and industry partners, serving as a trusted senior advisor.
* Lead project delivery from preconstruction through closeout — planning, constructability, logistics, procurement, staffing, and execution strategy.
* Champion integration of VDC/BIM processes to support constructability, coordination, and risk mitigation.
* Oversee turnover, commissioning, and closeout activities through successful project completion.

### **Skills, Knowledge and Expertise**

  

* 12\+ years of progressively responsible construction industry experience.
* Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Demonstrated success managing large or complex construction projects and project teams.
* Expert understanding of construction contracts, project controls, scheduling, procurement, cost management, and risk management.
* Advanced understanding of construction means and methods, constructability, VDC/BIM processes, and quality management systems.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and construction management platforms such as Procore, CMiC, and/or Navisworks.
* Strong leadership, negotiation, and relationship\-management skills, with the ability to build trust across clients, teams, and company leadership.
* OSHA 30\-Hour certification, or ability to obtain within established company timelines.

### **Benefits**

  

* Real leadership of large, complex projects — shaping delivery strategy from preconstruction through closeout, not just executing someone else's plan.
* Direct, daily involvement with your project team and clients in the San Fernando Valley — hands\-on leadership, not remote oversight.
* A clear seat at the table as a senior advisor to clients and company leadership.
* 100% employee\-owned (ESOP) company with a track record dating back to 1925 — your work has a direct stake in the outcome.
* Full benefits package: competitive pay, bonus program, medical/dental/vision insurance, PTO/sick leave, life insurance, 401(k) with match, and a student debt assistance program.
* Target annual bonus, plus a vehicle allowance or company vehicle (based on availability) and a fuel card.

Building Great Relationships since 1925! 100% employee\-owned general contractor. We build nationally, with locations in AZ, CA, CO, IL, TN, and TX.  

  

W.E. O'Neil Construction has seen steady growth since its founding in 1925 in Chicago by the O'Neil family. Now 100% employee\-owned (ESOP), we embrace people as our number one asset.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager and Acquisition Support
new_jobs.description:
Overview:

Stellar Solutions, a nationally recognized “Great Place To Work”, has exciting opportunities providing Engineering solutions for innovative new\-entrant space companies, as well as established space systems manufacturers, commercial space system operators and service providers, and other industry stakeholders including investors.  

At Stellar Solutions, we offer talented, energetic, and immediately productive resources to satisfy our customers’ critical needs in systems engineering and integration, mission operations, program management and strategic planning. We are a leading service and expertise provider for high\-tech commercial ventures, spanning communications, earth observation and remote sensing systems and data products, to the infrastructures that support earth orbiting and beyond earth orbit businesses.
Role/Responsibilities/Qualifications:

This role supports the U.S. Space Force’s Space Systems Command (SSC). You’ll anchor acquisition planning and execution for software\-intensive command\-and\-control capabilities in a fast\-moving, multi\-stakeholder environment.* Own acquisition strategy and execution for software\-intensive C2 increments: shape Request for Proposal (RFP) packages including Sections L (Instructions) and M (Evaluation), Statements of Work/Objectives (SOW/SOO), Contract Data Requirements Lists (CDRLs), and discriminator narratives tied to mission threads and operator needs
* Drive source selection: stand up evaluation plans, author Evaluation Notices (ENs), manage down\-select criteria, and prepare clear decision briefs through Source Selection Advisory Council/Authority (SSAC/SSA)

Plan the delivery runway: align the Integrated Master Plan/Schedule (IMP/IMS) to technical baselines and the Systems Engineering Plan / Test \& Evaluation Master Plan (SEP/TEMP) with clear gates (SRR PDR CDR* TRR/OT)
* Integrate cyber early: embed Risk Management Framework / Authority to Operate (RMF/ATO) evidence into acquisition artifacts and vendor deliverables
* Lead within an Integrated Product Team (IPT): synchronize Contracting (KO/PCO), Program Control (Earned Value Management and Schedule Risk Analysis), Systems Engineering \& Integration (SE\&I), Test, Cyber, and Ops/User representatives to keep risk visible and decisions timely
* Engage international partners as needed: translate priorities into actionable plans and coordinate transitions to Program Executive Offices for execution
* Communicate with clarity: brief status, risks, and trade\-offs to Product Managers/Branch Chiefs and portfolio leadership; produce high\-quality artifacts to tight timelines

**Required Skills:**  

* Bachelor’s degree
* 10\+ years of acquisition support on complex Department of Defense or Intelligence Community programs, with substantial experience on command\-and\-control, or mission\-system portfolios; 5\+ years program/project management
* Demonstrated ownership of RFP/SOW/Sections L\&M, source selection execution, IMP/IMS integration, and SEP/TEMP alignment for software\-intensive increments
* Stakeholder fluency across Program Executive Office/Program Management Office (PEO/PMO), Contracting (KO/PCO), SE\&I, Test, Cyber/RMF, and Operators; experience with International Partners is desired.

**Desired Skills \& Experience:**  

* Direct support to Space Systems Command (SSC) portfolios (current or planned capabilities)
* Prior work with Space C2 / ground (e.g., Satellite Control Network modernization) or adjacent portfolios such as ABMS/JADC2 (Department of the Air Force battle network) or Missile Defense Agency C2BMC
* Advanced degree; space acquisition background; mission\-partner/stakeholder relations

**Security Clearance \& Other Requirements:**  

* U.S. Citizen with Top Secret\\SCI Clearance and ability to obtain SAP access required
* Position location is El Segundo, CA – Note: Position is on\-site/hybrid and may require travel (\<20%) based on program need

**Compensation:**
The typical salary range for this position is USD $155,000 \- $185,000 per year. Individual pay is determined by many factors including work location, job\-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.  

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for a comprehensive total rewards package that includes an annual performance bonus, an employer\-funded Profit\-Sharing Plan (PSP) contribution based on base compensation, and comprehensive employer\-paid medical benefits, PTO pay\-out options, along with additional company\-sponsored benefits. All of these benefits represent an additional 30\-40% to your base compensation for a total compensation package.
Deliverable(s):

new_jobs.title: Sr Program Manager, Metrology
new_jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we're building rockets to serve today's needs and tomorrow's breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that's just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.



Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven't been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you're in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you'll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we're writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it's early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

**About the Team:**



The Reliability team at Relativity Space ensures quality is built into every stage of the Terran R design and production process, embedding reliability from the very beginning. The team works directly with design, manufacturing, test, and launch teams to stay close to the hardware, understand constraints, and proactively shape decisions. As the program moves from development into production and scaled operations, this is the time to establish the right processes, controls, and inspections without slowing progress. The team plays a key role in balancing risk, fostering a culture of ownership, and making sure speed never comes at the cost of reliability. Success means creating a quality system that scales with the Terran R program and Relativity as a whole.


**About the Role:**


* Manage all internal and external calibrations of electrical, mechanical, optical, and RF measurement equipment, and oversee calibration of precision test equipment using NIST\-traceable standards
* Drive multidisciplinary teams including metrology technicians, quality engineers, and operations personnel
* Define the long\-term calibration strategy and roadmap, including evaluation of bringing calibration capabilities in\-house
* Ensure vendors maintain compliance with ISO/IEC 17025, ANSI/NCSL Z540\.3, AS9100, and NASA requirements
* Provide expert technical guidance on metrology and calibration, ensuring integrity and accuracy of measurement data used for critical decision\-making
* Review calibration certificates and technical documentation, and maintain equipment tracking systems and calibration databases (e.g., Indysoft)


**About You:**


* 3\-5\+ years of progressive experience in metrology and calibration, with at least 1\-2\+ years in a program or project management role, preferably within aerospace, defense, or precision manufacturing
* Deep technical knowledge of calibration methods for electrical, mechanical, optical, and RF/microwave measurement equipment, dimensional metrology, and measurement uncertainty analysis and traceability principles
* Strong understanding of metrology standards including ISO/IEC 17025, ANSI/NCSL Z540\.3, AS9100, and NIST traceability requirements
* Proficiency with multimeters, oscilloscopes, pressure/temperature gauges, dimensional tools, and calibration databases. Working with hardware/instrumentation exposed to process gases/fluids.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate complex technical information to expert and non\-expert audiences
* Meticulous attention to detail and strong analytical skills


**Nice to haves but not required:**


* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Physics, Metrology, or a closely related technical field (or equivalent experience with 7\+ years in metrology/calibration)
* Experience establishing and scaling calibration programs from the ground up
* Self\-starter with demonstrated ability to define and own processes and roll them out through effective communication to diverse teams
* Familiarity with blueprint and schematic interpretation
* ASQ Certified Calibration Technician (CCT) or equivalent certification
* Strong knowledge of enterprise applications (PLM, ERP, MES) and proficiency in data analysis tools

**We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.**


***If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at*** ***accommodations@relativityspace.com******.***


***Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission \- via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee \- will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.***

Program Manager, Technology
new_jobs.description:
**About the company**

 **Brio Water Technology, a Home Organizers, Inc. company,** is a market leading water products brand that has helped millions stay hydrated through its unique and innovative product line. We offer full home water solutions designed to elevate the way people hydrate, combining sophisticated technology with modern, top tier design to deliver exceptional performance, customer satisfaction, and enhanced functionality. **Home Organizers, Inc.** is the parent organization behind a portfolio of well\-known home products and services brands, including Closet World, Closets by Design, Brio Water Technology, and others. With decades of experience supporting innovation, design, manufacturing, and customer focused solutions, Home Organizers helps its brands deliver high quality products and services that improve everyday living for households across the country. **About the role**  

As part of Home Organizers, Inc., Brio Water Technology is looking for a Program Manager, Technology to build the program governance, standards, and processes that do not yet exist within our technology organization. This is a foundational, hands\-on role for someone who walks into ambiguity and sees opportunity rather than a problem.  

This role is deliberately two jobs in one. As the business analyst, you define the problem, outline the scope, and make sure the solution fits what the business actually needs. As the program manager, you own the budget, hold the timeline, and deliver through the team. We are looking for someone who does both, and who knows which one a given moment calls for.  

The right person starts with people, not plans: they talk to our internal customers, learn their pain points, understand the current state, and use what they learn to design the processes and procedures we do not yet have. They are proactive by default. Wherever there is a compliance concern, an undocumented procedure, or a process with no owner, they step in, create clarity, and carry it until a permanent owner is in place. They do not wait to be assigned work; they find the gaps, close them, and hand them off.  

This person arrives with Agile coaching experience already in hand. As our teams mature and grow, they will take on Scrum Master duties and coach teams of varying size and experience. All of it requires influence without authority, and comfort operating alongside senior leaders and executives who hold deep institutional knowledge of how our systems actually behave. **Objectives of the role*** Establish the program governance, standards, and compliance foundation our technology organization does not yet have, in close partnership with internal stakeholders.
* Take ownership of gaps: compliance concerns, undocumented procedures, and unowned processes, creating clarity and carrying them until a permanent owner is in place.
* Lead cross\-functional technology programs end to end, from problem definition and requirements through delivery, coordinating teams and vendors outside your direct management chain.
* Take on the role of Scrum Master, Agile Coach, and business analyst for one or more teams as our organization matures.

 **What you'll do*** **Strategic planning.** Define the roadmap, goals, and long\-term vision for assigned programs, and sequence the work so near\-term delivery builds toward the target state.
* **Business analysis.** Define the problem before the solution is chosen. Elicit and document requirements, map current and future state, set scope, and write acceptance criteria, confirming that what gets built fits what the business actually needs.
* **Stakeholder communication.** Serve as the primary bridge between project teams, executives, and external partners. Run working sessions, keep everyone current on status, risks, and decisions, and work directly with stakeholders up to the executive level and with subject matter experts who hold deep institutional knowledge of how our systems behave.
* **Change management and adoption.** Many of our teams have worked in the same systems, using the same processes, for a very long time. Adoption here is earned, not announced. Communicate change early and often, brief the leadership of each area before rollout so their questions are answered ahead of go\-live, and provide the training and hands\-on support people need to work confidently in the new process. Success is measured by adoption, not by the go\-live date.
* **Program delivery.** Lead cross\-functional technology programs end to end: system implementations, migrations, and infrastructure initiatives, coordinating teams outside your direct management chain, including external vendors, internal business stakeholders, and technical SMEs.
* **Cross\-project coordination.** Manage interdependencies across concurrent projects, surface scheduling and resource conflicts early, and drive them to resolution.
* **Budget oversight.** Allocate resources, forecast expenses, and own budget adherence and variance tracking for assigned programs, including vendor software licensing, capital expenses for infrastructure upgrades, and cloud costs.
* **Risk management.** Identify roadblocks and risks early and implement corrective action. Maintain the risk register, change control process, policies and procedures, and audit\-ready documentation.
* **Governance and gap ownership.** Stand up program governance where none exists today. Proactively identify compliance concerns, undocumented procedures, and processes without a clear owner; create interim structure, carry ownership, and hand off to permanent owners once established.
* **Agile leadership.** Serve as Scrum Master for one or more Agile teams, coaching teams of varying size and maturity as the organization scales.

 **Qualifications*** 3\-5 years of program or project management experience, including managing individual program or project budgets between $250,000 and $1,000,000\.
* Cross\-functional IT program delivery: has led system implementati

* Works closely with the Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM), Cybersecurity Lead, system owners, and functional support/technical teams to protect computer networks, information systems, digital files, and critical electronic infrastructure
* Implements and monitors security controls, protocols, and procedures
* Protects networks, systems, information, and critical infrastructure
* Conducts vulnerability assessments, audits, risk reviews and rapid response reporting and data calls

* Prepares and maintains accreditation and compliance documentation

* Enables automated security checks at each stage of software delivery by integrating security controls, tools, and processes into the DevOps workflow
* Assists in the continuous integration, continuous delivery/deployment (CI/CD), continuous feedback, and continuous operations cycle

* Ability to work independently, self\-starter

 **EDUCATION**

**Allowable Substitution:** An additional 6 years of relevant work experience may be substituted for a Bachelor’s Degree, or 4 additional years of work experience with a relevant Associate’s Degree

At Pinkerton, the mission is to protect our clients. To do this, we provide enterprise risk management services and programs specifically designed for each client. The Intelligence Analyst, assigned to a specific client, will monitor open\-source intelligence (OSINT) software and various OSINT sources to proactively identify risks to company's facilities, traveling employees, and vehicle fleets. The Analyst plays a pivotal role in enhancing the client's overall security measures by conducting research, proactively identifying threats, contributing to the development of robust risk management procedures, and assisting with incident management. This role is encouraged to recommend and work towards continuous improvement and proactive measures to uphold the client's commitment to safety. **This is a temporary full\-time position for four months, which may be longer or shorter based on business needs.**

new_jobs.title: Physical Security Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
**Pivot Point Solutions**
=========================



Pivot Point Solutions is a California\-based consulting firm that delivers experienced field professionals to construction and utility organizations across the state. We partner with contractors, program owners, and utility clients to provide skilled inspection, construction management, and field support personnel who keep infrastructure projects safe, compliant, and on schedule.



Our team understands the demands of active construction environments, from underground gas and electric infrastructure to large\-scale utility programs. By pairing deep industry knowledge with a responsive, hands\-on approach, we help clients maintain quality, meet regulatory requirements, and keep field operations running smoothly on some of California's most critical infrastructure projects.


**Job Overview**
----------------


**Title:** Physical Security Project Manager  

**Sector:** Physical Security / Construction  

**Seniority:** Senior Level  

**Primary Locations:** Santa Cruz or Santa Clara, CA  

**Travel:** Occasional travel to Monterey and San Bernardino, CA  

**Job Type:** Hybrid – Office, Field \& Home  

**Contract Length:** 1 Year \+  

**Compensation:** $58\.00 \- $80\.00/hour


**Role Overview**
-----------------



Pivot Point Solutions is seeking an experienced Physical Security Project Manager to lead the planning and field execution of complex physical security and low\-voltage system projects throughout California. This role will oversee projects involving access control, video surveillance/CCTV, intrusion detection, perimeter protection, intercoms, and supporting electrical and low\-voltage infrastructure.



The ideal candidate brings at least seven years of relevant project management experience and a strong field construction background. This position requires someone who can move comfortably between project planning and active job sites, coordinate contractors and technical teams, evaluate installation conditions, manage budgets and schedules, and oversee testing and commissioning while maintaining disciplined project documentation and governance.


**Your Day\-to\-Day Activities**
--------------------------------


* Manage physical security and low\-voltage projects from planning and site assessment through installation, testing, commissioning, and closeout.
* Develop and maintain project plans, schedules, resource requirements, milestones, and project documentation.
* Conduct job walks and site assessments to validate design requirements, installation conditions, constructability, and project risks.
* Coordinate installation of access control, CCTV/video surveillance, intrusion detection, alarms, intercoms, perimeter security, and supporting infrastructure.
* Manage security integrators, subcontractors, technicians, vendors, and other project resources.
* Coordinate physical security activities with IT, Corporate Security, facilities, construction teams, and business stakeholders.
* Review construction drawings, wiring diagrams, technical specifications, and installation requirements.
* Coordinate procurement of equipment, materials, permits, and other resources necessary for project execution.
* Monitor field activities for safety, workmanship, quality, schedule adherence, and compliance with project requirements.
* Troubleshoot technical and construction issues and coordinate solutions with installation teams and stakeholders.
* Oversee inspection, functional testing, commissioning, and turnover of installed security systems.
* Maintain accurate project records, including risk and issue logs, change documentation, as\-built information, progress reports, and closeout packages.
* Track project budgets, labor hours, material costs, forecasts, and overall financial performance.
* Identify scope changes and coordinate appropriate change management and change order documentation.
* Provide structured project status reporting to project sponsors, clients, and internal stakeholders.
* Proactively identify project risks, dependencies, and field constraints and drive mitigation plans through resolution.
* Coordinate final project handoff to operations and support teams.

**The Job Requirements**
------------------------


* 7\+ years of relevant experience managing physical security, low\-voltage, electrical, or closely related field construction projects.
* Direct experience managing field installation projects involving physical security systems.
* Strong knowledge of access control, CCTV/video surveillance, intrusion detection, alarms, perimeter protection, or related security technologies.
* Experience working with enterprise access control or video management platforms such as AMAG, Software House, Genetec, or comparable systems.
* Strong understanding of low\-voltage construction and installation practices.
* Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, wiring diagrams, technical specifications, and related project documentation.
* Experience managing contractors, security integrators, technicians, vendors, and other field resources.
* Experience conducting site assessments, job walks, inspections, testing, and commissioning.
* Strong project management experience across scope, schedule, budget, risk, change, resources, and project documentation.
* Experience operating within structured PMO processes and maintaining project governance documentation.
* Strong communication, leadership, negotiation, and problem\-solving skills.
* Valid driver's license and ability to travel between project locations.
* Ability to work in active construction environments and wear required PPE, including FR clothing, hard hat, safety vest, and appropriate safety footwear.
* Ability to work a hybrid schedule across office, field, and home environments.
* Ability to support projects primarily in Santa Cruz and Santa Clara, with occasional travel to Monterey and San Bernardino.

**You'll Stand Out If You Have**
-------------------------

Our client’s Product Graphics team manages all on\-product artwork across their hardware portfolio—including brand identity, repairability, and regulatory compliance. They partner closely with Industrial Design, Product Safety \& Compliance, and Engineering to deliver seamless hardware experiences.


As a Product Graphics Program Manager, you will serve as the point of contact for end\-to\-end product graphics workflow, intake management, and project execution. * **Program Governance \& Execution**
* + Own and partner with client teams for end\-to\-end program life cycles across hardware development gates.
	+ **Track and manage the Product Graphics Worklog from creation to archive, proactively identifying risks, mitigations, and schedule dependencies.**
	+ **Build and maintain single\-source\-of\-truth program documentation, including Program Decks, Graphics trackers, DRI matrices, and CMF Process Sketchbooks.**
	+ **Drive early technical readiness testing, such as laser mark feasibility and compliance alignment, ensuring timely reviews and client partner sign\-offs.**
* **Cross\-Functional Leadership \& Communication**
* + Act as the central operational hub between our client’s Product Graphics Designers, Industrial Design (ID), CMF team, Hardware Engineering, Product Management, Compliance, and external manufacturing partners.
	+ Maintain an active in\-person presence to foster cross\-team client relationships, align stakeholder expectations, and drive consensus during critical build gates.
	+ Lead regular working sessions, track action items, and distribute clear, asynchronous program updates and status reports across global time zones.
	+ Represent the client team in critical meetings to track actions, milestones, and deliverables.
	+ Provide definitive resolution for program graphics decisions in the absence of cross\-functional alignment.
* **Process Strategy \& Operational Excellence**
* + Identify operational gaps in technical graphics workflows and build scalable, standardized frameworks to resolve bottlenecks.
	+ Drive quarterly task planning, backlog prioritization, and long\-term designer capacity and workload allocation.
	+ Manage physical sample requests, digital asset allocation, and procurement needs to support testing and client executive reviews.

**Knowledge, Skills \+ Experience**


Minimum Qualifications


* Bachelor’s degree in a technical or design\-related field, or equivalent practical experience
* 5\+ years of program or project management experience in hardware, product graphics, CMF, or consumer electronics
* Experience managing hardware development lifecycles and collaborating with manufacturing partners
  

Preferred Qualifications


* Proven track record of driving cross\-functional alignment across design, engineering, and compliance teams
* Deep technical understanding of manufacturing processes and capabilities, printing processes, and cosmetic finishing
* Strong organizational skills with proficiency in building clear decks, workflow trackers, and program frameworks
* Self\-starter capable of driving direction, resolving ambiguities, and influencing cross\-functional leadership without formal authority
* Ability to multitask, analyze opportunities, proactively solve problems and accomplish challenging objectives with minimal direction
* Effectively navigate and operate in a deadline\-driven, rapidly changing work environment
* Ability to maintain strict confidentiality
* Possesses a love of efficiency, the desire to produce a high\-quality deliverable, and an ability to execute against multiple projects in a technical work environment with often uncertain circumstances
  

For New York and California applicants: The salary range for this position is $130,000 to $150,000 annually. This range may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor.

The race to AI has become the race to power. Every breakthrough in artificial intelligence depends on one thing: access to electricity. new_jobs.title: Child Welfare Program Analyst (Human Services Analyst II) - Limited Term
new_jobs.description:
The Human Services Agency (HSA) of County of San Mateo is seeking qualified **Child Welfare Program Analyst (Human Services Analyst II)** to join the Children and Family Services (C\&FS) Branch. The CWPA will report to the Children and Family Services Administrative and Program Support Services Manager and will support **Child Welfare System Strategies and Contracted Services**.


The Child Welfare Program Analyst (CWPA) provides analytical, administrative, and project support for programs within Children and Family Services. This position requires independent judgment, strong organizational and analytical skills, and ideally a general knowledge of child welfare programs and practices. The CWPA may be assigned lead responsibility for projects and initiatives and will work closely with program managers, internal teams, community partners, and other stakeholders.


**CWS\-CARES Go\-Live:** A key responsibility of this position will be serving as the lead analyst as part of the Organizational Change Management Team for **CWS\-CARES**, the new child welfare Statewide case management system, scheduled to go\-live December 7, 2026\. Responsibilities will include developing and maintaining business process maps and implementation resources; providing on\-site and over\-the\-shoulder support during and after go\-live; maintaining SharePoint content and resource repositories; preparing communications, reports, and other project materials; and providing ongoing implementation support while adapting to evolving project needs, priorities, and timelines.


**Program Support and Contracted Services:** In addition to supporting CWS\-CARES implementation, the CWPA will work with Program Managers to develop and maintain a variety of documents, including, but not limited to, scopes of work, request for proposals, written reports, data reports, performance metrics, and County forms. The CWPA will receive and process invoices and help facilitate related signature and tracking processes.


Additional responsibilities may include conducting research and providing information to support management recommendations; supporting the integration of key initiatives and C\&FS priorities; communicating with community organizations regarding program requirements; working closely with community\-based service providers to support program compliance and provide technical assistance; developing service agreements; reviewing and interpreting State guidance and policies; and performing other duties as assigned.


The ideal candidate is a collaborative, organized, proactive, and adaptable professional who enjoys working as part of a team and can effectively navigate a fast\-paced and evolving environment. The successful candidate will be comfortable taking initiative, identifying what needs to be done, and stepping in to support the team without always being asked.


The **ideal candidate** will demonstrate:


* **Analytical and problem\-solving skills:** Ability to analyze information, identify issues, develop practical solutions, and make sound recommendations.
* **Project management and organization:** Ability to coordinate projects, manage competing priorities and deadlines, and follow through on assignments.
* **Communication:** Ability to communicate clearly and professionally and prepare concise, accurate written materials.
* **Initiative and adaptability:** Takes ownership, anticipates needs, and adjusts effectively to changing priorities and project needs.
* **Collaboration:** Works effectively with staff, managers, community partners, service providers, and other stakeholders.
* **Program and process knowledge:** Experience supporting the development, implementation, and improvement of programs and processes; general knowledge of child welfare or social service programs and practices is desirable.
**Duties may include, but are not limited to, the following:**


* Develop grants and contracts with the State and other funding sources, including the negotiation of specific items in the agreement and budget preparation.
* Draft requests for proposals, evaluate proposals and negotiate contracts.
* Provide technical programmatic and fiscal assistance to staff and subcontractors, including the development of policies and procedures and the training of staff.
* Monitor and evaluate the performance of subcontractors, including budget analysis and field monitoring, to ensure conformance with performance goals and fiscal requirements.
* Develop and implement marketing and funding strategies and policies and procedures for assigned programs; develop and monitor budgets.
* Represent assigned programs and the Agency at various meetings and conferences and serve as the liaison with the state and other organizations.
* Analyze legislation and develop policy and procedures for implementation by staff and subcontractors.
* Provide work direction to support staff.
* Collect, analyze and interpret various information, develop recommendations and present findings.
* Write reports and grant proposals and make presentations to boards, committees and other groups.
* Coordinate and conduct special events and projects.
* Develop and maintain computer files and generate reports.
* Perform related duties as assigned.

**Note: This is a limited\-term, at\-will assignment. Limited term employees are assigned to assignments not to exceed three years. They receive medical and dental benefits, similar to regular employees, and a defined contribution retirement plan. This recruitment may be used to fill future limited term positions.**


**Qualifications**
------------------


***Education and Experience:*** Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to qualify for a Human Services Analyst II is two years of experience performing journey level administrative and analytical duties in a human services or related agency.
